name: Maloti-Drakensberg Park
subtitle: A mixed property on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 2000.

parts.text: UNESCO describes the property in these words: “The Maloti-Drakensberg Park is a transnational property composed of the uKhahlamba Drakensberg National Park in South Africa and the Sehlathebe National Park in Lesotho. The site has exceptional natural beauty in its soaring basaltic buttresses, incisive dramatic cutbacks, and golden sandstone ramparts as well as visually spectacular sculptured arches, caves, cliffs, pillars and rock pools. The site's diversity of habitats protects a high level of endemic and globally important plants. The site harbors endangered species such as the Cape vulture (Gyps coprotheres) and the bearded vulture (Gypaetus barbatus). Lesotho’s Sehlabathebe National Park also harbors the Maloti minnow (Pseudobarbus quathlambae), a critically endangered fish species only found in this park. This spectacular natural site contains many caves and rock-shelters with the largest and most concentrated group of paintings in Africa south of the Sahara. They represent the spiritual life of the San people, who lived in this area over a period of 4,000 years.”

Wikipedia says the park was established on 11 June 2001 by linking Sehlabathebe National Park in Lesotho and the uKhahlamba Drakensberg Park in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. Its highest peak is Thaba Ntlenyana, 3,482 metres.
It describes the Drakensberg as the highest ground in the sub-region, with montane and sub-alpine ecosystems of globally significant diversity and high endemism.

The article also says the park holds the greatest gallery of rock art in the world, with hundreds of sites and many thousands of images painted by the San, and that the wider transfrontier area was conceived as a peace park of about 8,113 km², 64 percent of it in Lesotho.

gaps: San voices on the rock art and the landscape, and how Basotho and Zulu communities use the mountains.
How the two countries manage the park together, which the article summarises in one line.
